title: Library renovation funding and CUPE agreement approved
subtitle: Also: west-side operations centre study, hearing officers, construction communications, Good Roads nomination, and a public works business plan briefing.
overview: Council released $1,500,000 in design funding for the Albert McCormick Community Centre Sportsplex and McCormick library branch renovation {{vote:m9}}. It also approved a $75,000 feasibility study for a west-side satellite operations centre {{vote:m10}}. Both items were approved ahead of the 2024 budget.

Council ratified a settlement with CUPE Local 1542 covering 2024 to 2027 {{vote:m11}}. It appointed five hearing officers for administrative penalty and business licensing appeals and set their daily pay {{vote:m7}}. Council also directed staff to report on construction communications best practices as part of the annual accessibility update {{vote:m8}}. Residents should see clearer notice and safer walking routes around construction.

Council heard the 2024-2026 business plan for Integrated Planning and Public Works. Discussion covered the Beaver Creek Road reconstruction, planning staff needs under provincial housing rules, and road safety. Budget decisions come later. A report on declaring land on Millennium Blvd surplus was deferred to February 26, 2024. Council also supported a councillor's nomination to the Good Roads board {{vote:m12}}. The minutes report that Council met in closed session on a lease renewal, CUPE, an Enova update and a committee member matter.

decisions.detail: Council released $1,500,000 in 2024 funding, from the Capital Reserve Fund and the Library Expansion Reserve Fund, to begin design work {{vote:m9}}.
Council approved the terms of settlement with CUPE Local 1542 for January 1, 2024 to December 31, 2027 and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign {{vote:m11}}.

decisions.item: West side satellite operations centre study
decisions.detail: Council released $75,000 and directed staff to hire a consultant to assess feasibility on operational, health and safety and financial grounds {{vote:m10}}.
Council appointed five hearing officers for administrative monetary penalty and business licensing matters, with pay of $260 per half day or $520 per full day {{vote:m7}}.
Council received the best practices report and directed staff to include construction communications in the annual integrated accessibility update {{vote:m8}}.
Council approved the mid-term recruited committee appointments and enacted a by-law to appoint the recommended members {{vote:m6}}.
Council supported the nomination of Councillor Diane Freeman to the 2024-2025 Good Roads Board of Directors {{vote:m12}}.

debate: On the public works business plan, the finance chair said residents are struggling with the cost of living and urged colleagues to identify budget items they would defer or drop. A councillor asked what risks come with each optional item.

On a proposed crossing guard supervisor position, staff said recruiting and retaining guards is difficult and the work currently falls on one manager. Without the position, staff said, Vision Zero road safety work would be diluted.

On Beaver Creek Road, councillors worried about how to pay for the project and about uncertain provincial rules on recovering development charges. Staff said they were pursuing risk-sharing with developers and a possible provincial grant, and that the issue would not affect the three-year tax increase. Staff expected to report back on budget day.
Staff said provincial timelines for planning applications mean application fees must be refunded if decisions are late. They presented added planners as a way to meet those deadlines.

On the McCormick renovation, councillors asked about consolidating kitchen space, the placement of the washroom beside the quiet room, and solar readiness. Staff said these would be reviewed in schematic design, with the full-scope option depending on lower costs or added funding.
